elements.name: intro_text
elements.html:
Title of the study: How do people perceive LLM answers?


Welcome and thank you for your interest!


This survey is part of a Bachelor's thesis at Technische Universität Berlin Faculty IV, supervised by Prof. Dr.-Ing. Sebastion Möller .
The study investigates how people perceive the answers of Large Language Models (LLMs), i.e. AI chatbots in terms of intelligence, trust, the need to verify information, warmth and discomfort.


Study Procedure

You will read 16 short conversations between a user and different LLMs. After each conversation, you will answer a few questions about how you perceive the LLM. Please answer every single question by clicking the option that best matches your impression.

There are no right or wrong answers, we are interested in your personal impressions and opinions. At the end of the survey you will receive further information about the background of the study.

The survey takes approximately 25 minutes. A progress bar shows how far along you are. Please complete the survey in one sitting and without interruptions.


Voluntary participation

Your participation is entirely voluntary. You may stop at any time without giving a reason and without any disadvantage, simply by closing the browser window. Data will only be saved or used, if you press the Submit button at the end.


Data protection

The survey is anonymous. We do not ask for your name, e-mail address or any other directly identifying information, and we do not store your IP address in the data set. For each completed survey we store your answers together with a randomly generated ID (UUID Version 4), the time of submission, time you needed to complete the survey and the order in which the conversations were shown. These data cannot be linked to you.

This web page is hosted on GitHub Pages (GitHub, Inc., USA). When you submit the survey, your answers are transmitted via SheetDB (Poland, EU) and stored in a Google Sheet (Google LLC, USA). GitHub and Google are certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework and additionally rely on standard contractual clauses. Technical data such as your IP address may be processed by these providers to deliver the page and transmit your answers. We have no access to this information and do not use it.


Data storage, sharing and publication of anonymized data

Your answers are used exclusively for scientific purposes, i.e. the Bachelor's thesis and possible related publications, and may be used for further research. The processing is based on your consent (Art. 6 (1)(a) GDPR).

Your answers are anonymous and will be stored for at least 2 years. They may be shared with other researchers and published in anonymized form. They cannot be traced back to you. For this reason, they cannot be deleted individually after you submit the survey. If you close the browser window before pressing Submit, no data is stored.


Possible risks

No risks beyond those of everyday computer use are expected. If you feel uncomfortable at any point, you can stop at any time.


Compensation

There is no compensation for participating in this study.


Contact

For questions about the study, please contact Marcel Riedel at m.riedel.1@campus.tu-berlin.de

elements.name: ex_instructions
elements.html:
Example: How to answer this survey


Before you start, here is one practice example you dont't have to complete so you know what to expect. Each conversation in this survey works like this:


  1. Read the conversation between the user (blue) and the LLM (grey) carefully.
  2. Rate the LLM on the five scales (e.g. Incompetent – Competent) by clicking the circle that best matches your impression. 1 is closest to the left word, 7 is closest to the right word.
  3. Indicate how much you agree with each statement about trust, checking the answer, and the behavior of the chatbot, from "Strongly disagree" to "Strongly agree".

There are no right or wrong answers. We are interested in your personal impression. In the real survey, every question has to be answered before you can continue. Some conversations are short checks of whether you are reading carefully, so please read every conversation and statement. Your answers on this example page are not part of the evaluation.

elements.name: debriefing_text
elements.html:
Thank you for your participation!


Debriefing

You have completed all conversations. Below we explain the background of the study, including some information we could not give you beforehand. Please read it before you submit.


Study Background

The study investigates how people perceive an LLM depending on how it reacts when a user expresses doubt or states their own (possibly wrong) opinion. We measured how this affects the perceived intelligence, trustworthiness, whether people feel the need to check the answer themselves, discomfort and warmth.


What we could not tell you in advance

The conversations were not entirely live chats and parts were written in advance by the researchers, and several of them contained deliberately incorrect statements. The LLM was prompted to agree with the user.Please do not treat the content of the conversations as factual information.


Ethical aspects

  • Incomplete disclosure: The omission described above was necessary for the research question. We consider the risk for you to be minimal, as the topics were everyday general-knowledge questions.
  • Voluntary participation: You took part voluntarily and could and still can stop at any time without disadvantage.
  • Ethical review: Self-disclosure survey at Faculty IV, Technische Universtität Berlin

Confidentiality

If you know people who might take part in the study, please do not share the details of this debriefing with them until the study is finished, as this could influence their answers.


Questions or concerns

If you have any questions, or if anything in the study made you uncomfortable, please contact Marcel Riedel at m.riedel.1@campus.tu-berlin.de. Please click Submit below to finish the survey.
